Subject: Renewal & expansion: dedicated GPUs + throughput SLA (follow-up)

Hi Karthik,

Hope you’re well — our board asked us to firm up capacity commitments ahead of our FY27 planning. We’re ready to move forward with a 24-month renewal but need to expand our Dedicated pool from 8 reserved GPUs to 24 (steady-state, with a 6-month ramp). Key asks from our side: 

- 24-month term with price protection
- Reserved pool for up to 24 GPUs (16 additional) with a 30 TPS throughput target for our batch jobs
- A commercial concession to offset the first-quarter ramp costs — ideally a one-time credit or month(s) free on the new capacity

Attached is our updated capacity forecast (Nimbus_capacity_proposal_v3.xlsx) and our redlines on the MSA (Nimbus_MSA_redlines.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a concession at renewal and what that would look like? If useful, we can schedule a 30-min call this week.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Infrastructure
Nimbus Analytics

Quick answers up front: we can do a 24-month price-protected renewal and provision the additional reserved GPUs, and we’ll validate the throughput target against the workload profile. I want to confirm a couple of details before pulling legal/finance into an approval flow:

- Is the 30 TPS target a peak or sustained SLA? (Your forecast indicates burst windows.)
- The 6-month ramp: are you expecting linear ramping (4 GPUs/month) or front-loaded?

If you’re free, I can set a 30-min call with our CS and SRE leads later today. In the meantime I’m looping in Marissa and Priyom to start the commercial thread (and capture any precedent on renewal concessions).

Subject: INTERNAL: Nimbus renewal — concession request and numbers

Team — quick summary and ask: Alyssa (Nimbus) wants to renew for 24 months and expand Dedicated from 8 -> 24 GPUs with a 6-month ramp. They are asking for a commercial concession to offset ramp costs. Numbers below (proposal v3 attached by customer):

- New committed GPUs: +16 (total 24)
- List price per GPU / month (our standard): $4,500
- Incremental monthly ACV: 16 * $4,500 = $72,000 (monthly); annualized incremental ACV ≈ $864,000
- Term: 24 months -> total incremental contract value ≈ $20.7M over term (before discounts)

Customer asks: one-time concession (months free) or credit to offset first quarter. They’ve signaled that the concession will determine whether they sign 24 months or choose a 12-month with higher flexibility.

Suggested concession options for internal discussion:
A) One month free on the incremental capacity (equivalent to ~$72k) — lowest-impact, quick close
B) One-time credit equal to 10% of first-year incremental ACV (~$86k) — larger but shows partnership
C) 2 months free or 15% credit — requires exec approval given size (~$144k)

Ask: Marissa/Prioym/Rishi — please advise what we can approve at AE level vs. what needs leadership sign-off. If we need exec sign-off, I’ve highlighted option C as the ask I’d like to escalate. I’ve attached the customer files for reference.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the clear breakdown. My read: this is a good retention + expansion motion and we should push for 24 months. Approval guidance:

- AEs can approve up to one month free on incremental capacity (Option A) without further sign-off.
- Anything that gives >1 month free or >10% of first-year incremental ACV needs VP/GM approval (Laura) and finance confirmation for revenue recognition/crediting.

Recommendation: propose Option B (10% of first-year incremental ACV ~ $86k) to the customer as a counter, but indicate that it requires VP/GM approval; in parallel, offer Option A as an immediately available sweetener to accelerate signature. If they press for Option C we escalate.

I’ll prep a short note for Laura outlining business rationale and strategic value (expansion, reference customer, potential marketplace showcase).

Marissa Cole

Subject: Escalation: approval request for Nimbus renewal concession (deal RDW-8247)

Laura — quick ask and context. Nimbus Analytics (RDW-8247) is ready to commit to a 24-month renewal but only if we provide a meaningful concession on the expansion (8 -> 24 GPUs). The incremental first-year ACV is ~ $864k. They’re asking for a one-time ramp concession.

Why it matters:
- Strategic account with marketplace potential; very happy with our latency/cost performance
- Likely $20M+ booked over 24 months if we close the 24-month term now

What I’d like to approve if possible: Option C from the internal thread — 15% of first-year incremental ACV (~$130k-$135k) OR 2 months free on incremental capacity. This is larger than standard but accelerates the close and reduces the risk they fall back to 12 months.

Risks/Conditions:
- Any concession above 10% requires finance to OK revenue treatment and legal to clear MSA redlines
- We should tie the concession to a signed 24-month commitment and DocuSign envelope (no verbal promises)

I’ve attached the customer forecast and their MSA redlines. Happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Team — reviewed the numbers and the strategic rationale. I’m comfortable approving a one-time concession up to 12% of first-year incremental ACV plus one month free on incremental capacity, contingent on: 

1) Signed 24-month term via DocuSign (no partial commitments)
2) Finance (Rishi) confirms revenue recognition / crediting approach and any deferred revenue impact
3) Legal OKs MSA changes (I don’t want unexpected liability)

Operational notes: Marissa — please draft the customer-facing concession language (showing Option: 12% credit + 1 month free as final offer) and include the exact dollar credit and how it will appear on the first invoice. Karthik — confirm the DocuSign envelope and get the customer to confirm the sustained vs. peak SLA for the 30 TPS item. 

If those three check boxes are green, consider this an approval to proceed and close. Great work moving this forward.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
